subject.title: ClawSec security banner wording is inaccurate and not actionable

question: Which ClawSec or security-context surface should own this blocked-action copy, and should it be rewritten to match current `/approve`/native approval flows or treated as obsolete because current main no longer emits it?
rationale: The report is about security guidance for confirmable versus permanently blocked actions; changing or removing that wording affects how users understand approval boundaries and needs owner intent before an automated repair.

options.title: Audit And Patch The Exact Security Copy
options.body: Find the real ClawSec/session-context source, align it with current native approval and `/approve` behavior, and have security/UX review the final text.

options.title: Confirm Obsolete And Close Later
options.body: If maintainers can prove the quoted banner is from an old or external surface, close only after linking that proof and the current replacement wording.

options.title: Delegate Exec Prompt Cleanup To The Open PR
options.body: Let the open exec prompt PR handle only its overlapping approval-pending wording and keep this issue for any separate ClawSec banner source.

recommendation.title: Audit And Patch The Exact Security Copy
recommendation.body: Find the real ClawSec/session-context source, align it with current native approval and `/approve` behavior, and have security/UX review the final text.

likelyOwner.reason: The closest merged provenance for approval fallback and prompt wording is steipete's prior fix, and the decision is security-boundary sensitive.
